title: burst-smoothing-and-amortization-lab
summary: Back-of-envelope experiments for smoothing bursty usage into predictable unit economics. Focus: session bundles, GPU->token amortization, and simple heuristics for credit decay.
body:
Purpose / context:
- quick personal scratchpad: try to turn a bursty interactive UX into something that sales/finance can sell as predictable commit + payg mix. not polished.
- Use-case: chat app with heavy tail bursts (daily active but sporadic long sessions). want to avoid overcommitting to huge reserved capacity.

Assumptions (baseline numbers i keep tweaking):
- Model family: small-footprint 7B/8B quantized variant (we'll call M-s).
- Serving throughput (avg, single-request): 200 tokens/sec generation per GPU (conservative for 8-bit quantized on A10x).
- Avg session: 4 turns, prompt 120 tokens avg, response 380 tokens avg => ~2000 tokens/session (round numbers).
- GPU cost (blended infra): $3.50 / GPU-hour (includes infra, ops, amortized overhead).
- Useful tokens per GPU-hour (no batching): 200 tps * 3600s = 720k tokens/hr (generation only).
- Cost per 1k generated tokens (gen only) = ($3.50 / 720k) * 1000 = $0.00486 per 1k tokens.
- Add overhead (prompt tokens, KV cache transfer, RPC, small margin): assume +40% -> $0.0068 per 1k tokens (rounded $0.007).

Quick sanity check vs market:
- If we price hosted 1k-gen-tokens at $0.02 -> margin still big vs raw infra. fine for intro tiers.
- For large context or slower models, this increases a lot. use this only for baseline M-s.

Burst smoothing idea (high level):
- Offer customers 2 components: committed retainer (monthly $) that buys guaranteed concurrent capacity (or credits) + payg credits that decay for sessions.
- Convert retainer into session-capacity-equivalents (SCE): how many concurrent long sessions can they sustain for 95th percentile.
- Keep payg priced in credits that map to tokens with a conversion rate that increases for burst time windows (latency premium).

Heuristics / conversions to try in experiments:
1) Session-credit (SC) definition: 1 SC = covers 1 session of 2k tokens (generation+prompt) at baseline model.
   - 1 SC -> 2k tokens -> at $0.007/1k => cost ~= $0.014 (raw infra) -> we'd retail SC at e.g. $0.06 (4.3x markup) for starter tiers.
2) Bulk-credit discount: 10k SC pack (20M tokens) -> give 25% discount off per-SC list price.
3) Time-decay / warm-cache bonus: if same user/session within 5m, next session SC cost reduced by 40% (cache reuse).
4) Burst-smoothing pool: unused retainer SCs can be borrowed by other tenants in same org for short bursts; penalties apply when over threshold.

Concrete numbers: (playable)
- Starter free: 5 SC / month (10k tokens).
- Basic: $25/mo -> 500 SC (1M tokens).
- Growth: $250/mo -> 6k SC (12M tokens) + 10% bulk discount for extra purchases.
- Enterprise retainer: price by SCE (concurrency) and SLA; e.g., $6k/mo -> 50 concurrent SCE (back of envelope).

Amortization math (detailed):
- If we run heavy batching / continuous inference, throughput can be 2-3x -> effective token/hr up to 2.5M tokens/hr -> cost per 1k goes down to $0.0014. but violates latency SLO for interactive UX.
- Choose a blended factor for typical work: 1.6x from batching across customers -> effective cost per 1k tokens becomes $0.0043 -> add 35% ops margin -> $0.0058.
- So in price ranges $0.005->$0.02 per 1k for different tiers is plausible.

Edge cases & levers to protect economics:
- Minimum per-request token charge (e.g., 10 tokens) to avoid DDOS/micros at scale.
- Latency premium: realtime (<300ms) requests cost extra.
- Long-context surcharge: token count >8k triggers +x2 pricing.
- Cold-start penalty: if request hits a model variant not warmed by recent traffic, levy small extra credit to account for KV rehydration.

Open questions / experiments to run:
- What is realistic cache-hit uplift for multi-turn conversation in our telemetry? if we can show 30-50% reuse, session pricing moves materially. (TODO: query telemetry -> PRIC-712).
- How to present to customers: credits -> easier, but non-intuitive conversion; sessions -> easier mental model but hides variance. run A/B with 20 pilot customers.
- Elastic small-burst policy: let customers define burst window (X min) with higher unit price vs longer-term retainer. test 3 windows: 5m, 30m, 2h.
- Sizing guides: produce cheatsheets for sales: "for 10k monthly active users with avg 2 sessions/day and 2k tokens/session -> estimate X plan". build a quick calc sheet.

Quick sales cheat (back of envelope):
- 10k MAU * 2 sessions/day * 2k tokens/session * 30 days = 1.2B tokens/month.
- At $0.007/1k tokens -> infra cost = 1.2M * 0.007 = $8,400/mo. (confirm calc: 1.2B tokens /1k = 1.2M units).
- Add 30% ops & margin -> list price target ~ $12k/mo.

Low-touch starter anchoring:
- Free tier + clear starter pack: e.g. $50 for 10M tokens (anchor) -> simple entry. 10M tokens at $0.02/1k => $200 list, but $50 intro is loss-leader. pick $75? test both.

UX notes (how to present):
- Show tokens as "session credits" for chat products. allow conversion show/hide.
- Add meter in Console with predicted monthly burn and recommended retainer.
- Provide slider: "expected concurrent sessions" -> outputs SCE and price.

Short-term experiments (next 6 weeks):
- [x] build spreadsheet calculator with parametrized throughput and cache reuse (Eli).
- [ ] run telemetry query for session token distribution last 90d (PR: GH#58) (Priya)
- [ ] mock pricing page copy A/B: credits vs sessions (internal pilot 10 customers)
- [ ] confirm GPU-hour blended cost with infra finance (ask @finance:infra).

Notes to self: keep unit conversions visible in docs; avoid hidden multipliers. sales need simple heuristics.

Random ideas (brain dump):
- "time-limited pack" (e.g. 30-day burst pack) priced higher than monthly packs; good upsell for seasonal spikes.
- pre-commit for latency priority: customers pay to jump priority queue during bursts (cheap to implement if we have routing tiers).
- auto-convert leftover monthly SC -> discounted payg credits (prevents waste).

Questions for design review:
- how to visualize decaying credits when a session continues across days? stake policy (session anchored to start date vs usage date).
- should we expose separate metering for prompt tokens vs generated tokens? simplifies unit econ for customers who care about cost-per-output.

Bottom line (current leaning):
- Start with simple Session Credits (2k token baseline) + bulk discounts + small number of clearly named surcharges (latency, long-context).
- Keep payg token price visible for power users.
- Build sales cheat calculators and SCE conversion for enterprise.

-- end of scratchpad --

Unresolved: mm, need better numbers on batching uplift and realistic GPU/hr blended cost. put high priority on instrumentation query.
